author: exgidi
quote:
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 earns its place among the greatest games ever made by pairing a haunting, French-art-inspired story with a turn-based combat system that demands real-time reflexes. Developed by Sandfall Interactive with a lean team and a modest budget, it delivers an unforgettable, tightly paced experience that trusts the player's intelligence.

At the heart of Expedition 33 is a premise that hits like a gut punch: a godlike figure called the Paintress paints a number on a monolith each year, and everyone of that age fades away. Playing as members of Expedition 33 trying to break this cycle, you experience a story that balances bleak dread with genuine warmth, humor, and grief.

Instead of handing out easy answers, the narrative forces you to wrestle with moral gray areas, sacrifice, and what "victory" actually costs. Strong performances—including Charlie Cox as Gustave and Jennifer English as Maelle—give every quiet conversation and devastating twist real weight.

Traditional turn-based RPGs can sometimes feel passive, but Expedition 33 injects adrenaline into every encounter. You still plan builds, manage resources, and use each party member's distinct mechanics—like Monoko's ability to take on defeated foes' attacks—but you also dodge, jump, and parry incoming hits in real time.

Landing a well-timed parry doesn't just save your skin; it can nullify damage, build Action Points, and set up counterattacks. That blend of planning and split-second execution keeps battles tense from the first hour to the credits.

Visually, Expedition 33 looks like a painting brought to life. Drawing on French art history and surrealist imagery, its world shifts from **** cities and submerged ruins to twisted landscapes that make you feel small in the best possible way.

The art direction doesn't rely on bloated open-world filler; it sets a mood and keeps moving. Paired with a soaring, emotional soundtrack—highlighted by tracks like Renoir's battle theme—the presentation makes even routine exploration feel sacred.

Expedition 33 succeeds through sheer conviction. It proves a focused, passionate team can rival blockbuster spectacles by caring deeply about tone, pacing, and emotional payoff. When the credits roll, it doesn't just leave you with a high score; it leaves you thinking about the choices you made and the people you lost along the way.

author: exgidi
quote:
Disapppointing. 30 fps, which drops to 20-25 even on Pro, constant crashes and glitches.

The story is bland, it doesn't feel like GTA at all, but a modern, **** version of RDR 2. 

The characters are horribly written, Jason is a doormat who simps for Lucia, a woman who dumped him and lost their child.

I had a lot of expectations and hoped for a great Bonnie and Clyde story, but it's just a badly written, boring, bland, doormat simulator. It's Sims 6 not GTA 6.
